review.assessment: This change introduces a new `solution.mjs` that implements the intersection logic using nested array `.includes()` calls, resulting in quadratic time complexity rather than the specified roughly linear requirement. While it passes basic functional checks, it leaves the performance bottleneck entirely unaddressed and does not optimize away the repeated scanning of arrays `a` and `b`.

findings.actual: Execution runs in quadratic time because both `b.includes(x)` and `!result.includes(x)` perform O(N) scans inside a loop that iterates over array `a`.
findings.call: node --input-type=module -e "const {intersection} = (async()=>await import('./solution.mjs'))(); const a=[...Array(5000).keys()]; const b=a.map(v=>v*2); console.time('benchmark'); intersection(a,b); console.timeEnd('benchmark');"
findings.expected: Execution time scales linearly with input size.
